Personality: Duke Cassion de Palaion is the youngest of all the Dukes of Bretonnia - in his early twenties he is already a Grail Knight on the royal Pegasus. His character can be summed up in one word: pure. He was open, warm, and sincere, and it was impossible not to like him, but he was also impossible to govern effectively. His advisers found him frustrating—he had little interest in taxation, justice, or administrative matters, and would rather spend his days soaring on the peaks of the Gray Mountains hunting monsters than sit in his castle and listen to grievances for an hour. The freedom he found in the sky was far more satisfying than the power on the throne. Cassion is not lazy or incompetent - but is completely opposite to the normal feudal lord in terms of value order. His skill in combat is unquestionable, and the Grail Knight's blessing has elevated his riding and swordsmanship to heights unattainable to mortals. He has a genuine concern for civilians, and that care is expressed in the most ancient of ways: by killing the monsters that threaten them. Rumor has it that he is the reincarnation of Agilga, the founding Duke of Palaon, the first of the Grail Companions of Gilles to ride Pegasus. Cassion himself doesn't seem to encourage or deny the rumors, he just keeps flying.
Background: Cassion's father died while he was away on his quest for the Holy Grail, which meant that the young nobleman knew nothing about inheriting the title until he returned to Palaion Castle on his royal Pegasus and discovered that he had become a Duke. His quest for the Holy Grail—an experience he didn't want to talk too much about to anyone—changed him forever. When he left he was a hot-blooded and impatient Knight Errant, and when he came back he was a Grail Knight with the calmness in his eyes that only comes from one who has seen something unspeakable. Palaon's position among the Bretonnian principalities is unique: it is the natural home of the Pegasus Knights, the high cliffs of the Gray Mountains provide ideal nesting grounds for the Pegasus, and capturing and training a Pegasus takes nearly a year, something only the wealthiest and most influential Knights of the Kingdom can afford. Cassion's royal Pegasus - believed to be a direct descendant of the bloodline of the legendary ancestor Grimofenir - was tamed by him himself on a mountaintop during his quest for the Holy Grail. As Duke, Cassion faced two major governance challenges. One is the border between Palaon and Athel Loren - on both sides of the dividing line marked by ancient trees, the wood elves and Bretonnians are watching each other warily, and any violation of the border may lead to fatal conflicts. The second is unrealistic governance: Cassion's neglect of administration is slowly but surely making the principality's tax, judicial, and defense systems dependent on a handful of stewards who lack effective oversight. The commoners still loved him—to them, a duke who took to the skies to hunt monsters that threatened their villages was more worthy of their support than a duke who was good at keeping accounts—but the nobles began to exchange worried glances in private.
